evidence.description: Table 9 regression columns and notes, original PDF p. 23

review_notes: Source-first baseline choice: the paper labels January 10, 2002 document shredding as the primary market-reaction event. Table 9’s two Jan10-specific cross-sectional regressions directly test the Houston-office and fee determinants for that event, using the two- and three-day CAR windows. The underlying full event-study mean/sign tests are not regressions and were not converted into equations. The Feb. 4 date-specific columns, pooled two-date columns, and other event/switching/industry-portfolio analyses are follow-up comparisons and were excluded from this single principal regression family.

The Jan10 CAR dependent variables require firm-specific expected returns from the market model; that per-firm fitted return model is retained as a supporting construction. The event-period CAR is a deterministic sum of abnormal returns, not another regression.

Needs review: underlying estimators are not named; Table 9 gives t-values without specifying the standard-error correction or clustering; the market-model estimation window and per-firm daily N are unreported; Salegrow’s exact computation is not stated; and the Afee numerator wording conflicts across the sample description, Table 2, and Table 9.
results_review_notes: Table 9 contains the selected January 10-only baseline columns; the February 4 columns and pooled two-date fits are excluded.

Table 2 supplies fee components and total assets, and Table 5 supplies broader-sample CAR means. No direct descriptive summaries for sales growth or leverage were located in the relevant descriptive tables/sections searched (pages 10, 13–15 and 23).

The exact Afee numerator is unresolved: the source uses “total audit fee” while its sample discussion describes audit, information-systems and other-fee components and Table 2 distinguishes Audit fee from Total fee.
The Table 2 dollar fee rows are raw fiscal-2000 amounts, not the fee-to-assets ratios used in Table 9; total assets are a broader-sample denominator component.

Table 8 distribution summaries for the selected CAR outcomes are retained in a separate group at the authors’ decimal-return scale; Table 5 reports the same window means as percentages. No arithmetic scale conversion was applied.

calculation_provenance.policy: strict; no guessed degrees of freedom or normal approximations
